solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl involves most of cast in stitch up

indicators.note: to involve something is to wrap it inside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a common girl's name

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it bar its final letter, so the tail is dropped

parts.note: to cast, as in casting an eye or a glance, is to turn it

explanation.surface: A young woman manages to bring most of the theatrical company into a stitch-up, a scheme to frame someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors in a play, but it is the verb, as in casting or turning one's eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon closing a wound sews it shut with stitches, which is exactly the verb's medical meaning.

clue.text: Surprised when Dawn went first

parts.note: dawn is the start or beginning of something
whoever went first led the way

explanation.surface: Someone was taken aback when a woman called Dawn got in ahead of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn looks like a woman's name, but it is the beginning of the day, and so any start.
explanation.definitionFit: Being startled means being given a sudden shock, an everyday synonym for being taken by surprise.

clue.text: Miner injured in gallery gets cut off

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the name of the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery

indicators.note: a body that is injured is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A miner hurt in an underground gallery finds himself trapped and cut off from the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: A gallery is also a mine passage, which is why the surface reads so naturally. The Tate is London's national gallery of art.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to end it abruptly, as when a call or a supply is cut off.

clue.text: Revolutionary bishop ejected from dance

indicators.note: whatever is ejected is thrown out, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a rebel rises up against authority
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A firebrand churchman is thrown out of a party for his radical views.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking B out of REBEL leaves REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance, here named by its general category.

clue.text: Unfriendly measures lead to loss of confidence

parts.note: a cold manner is unfriendly
feet are units of length

explanation.surface: Hostile policies leave people feeling nervous and unsure of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a sudden attack of nerves that makes someone back out of a planned commitment.

clue.text: University model suitable to be assimilated by large business organisations

indicators.note: what is assimilated is absorbed into something else, so these letters go inside

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the clothing label for large
standard abbreviation
the Model T was Ford's famous car
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: A university's plan proves suitable for adoption by big companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large' seems to describe the business organisations but belongs to the wordplay as the clothing-size label for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfit is informal for a company or group of people working together, so firms and enterprises qualify.

clue.text: Disgraceful when Dicky spied on a cabinet minister

indicators.note: something dicky is shaky or unsound, so the following letters are out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
Vince Cable was Business Secretary in the coalition cabinet

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky snooping on a government minister is a shameful business.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky reads as a man's name; it is British slang for unsound or wobbly. Vince Cable sat in the 2010 to 2015 coalition cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Despicable behaviour deserves contempt, the same moral judgement as calling it shameful or a disgrace.

clue.text: It's not strictly necessary for a spear-carrier

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something additional, beyond what is needed
second meaning: a walk-on actor with no lines

explanation.walkthrough: A spear-carrier is the classic non-speaking role in opera or drama, holding a spear in the background.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a surplus item and a background performer hired to fill out a crowd scene.

clue.text: Story broadcast about English commune

indicators.note: about means around, so the mixed letters surround the single letter
seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A tale aired on the radio concerns a rural English community.
explanation.definitionFit: Troyes is a historic town in Champagne, and the commune is the basic unit of local government in France.

clue.text: Soldiers carrying spades seen by girl's grave

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the card suit
a girl's name
the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Troops with shovels are spotted beside a young woman's burial plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a noun for a burial place, picking up spades; it is the adjective. RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and grave both describe a serious, solemn manner or a dangerous situation, so they are adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Article on King George taking drugs reportedly intended to create understanding

parts.note: the indefinite article
Georgius Rex, the royal cipher
E is ecstasy, so two doses are EE

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece claims a monarch's drug use was designed to promote mutual understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is Georgius Rex, King George's royal cipher, and E is ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement is a mutual understanding or arrangement reached between parties.

clue.text: Scrap books returned to collection earlier

parts.note: a set is a collection of things

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the abbreviation reads backwards

parts.note: Old Testament, a collection of biblical books

explanation.surface: Discard the books that were given back to a library collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb meaning throw away; it is a noun for a fight. 'Earlier' puts the collection before the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief fight or argument, and a scrap is an informal word for the same brawl.

clue.text: Bottom's dog

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the rear or end part of something
second meaning: to follow someone closely

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the dog belonging to Bottom, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for the rear end and a verb for shadowing someone, as a detective does.

clue.text: It's lawful to run away with a friend

parts.note: to leg it is slang for running off
a means one, written as the Roman numeral
mate is an informal word for a friend

explanation.surface: Eloping with a companion is perfectly allowed by law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A friend' looks like one unit, but the article is split off as the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate conforms to the rules and is permitted by law, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sort of animal pit discovered after a time

parts.note: a pig is a farm animal
an eon is a vast period of time
a pit is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: Some kind of creature's den is unearthed after a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like a vague hedge; 'Sort' alone is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole things is to classify them into categories, as letters are filed in a desk's compartments.

clue.text: Former military leader found in River Test

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so one name is placed within the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
Idi Amin, the army officer who ruled Uganda

explanation.surface: An ex-general turns up in the Test, a famous Hampshire trout river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a real English river, which makes 'River Test' look like one name; 'Test' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect or test it closely, as a doctor or an examiner does.

clue.text: Hard to get Mark to church

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
Church of England

explanation.surface: A man called Mark is reluctant to go to services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to get Mark to church' reads as an unwilling churchgoer, but Mark is a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce goods are in short supply, so obtaining them takes real effort.

clue.text: Stop working when circus employee catches nasty dose

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it inside, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: a clown works in a circus

indicators.note: a nasty dose is a bad one, and bad here signals letters gone wrong

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A circus performer has to take time off after picking up a bad illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory or business that closes down ceases operating, so it stops working altogether.

clue.text: Managed to get extremely competitive after hospital department's opening

parts.note: ear, nose and throat
to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters stay

parts.note: the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A hospital unit's launch made rivals fiercely competitive.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT, ear nose and throat, is a standard hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance is a way in such as a door or gate, so it is a noun synonym for an opening.

clue.text: Slacken by end of race after initially running a fast time

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the next word, so only its first letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: An athlete eases off near the finish after setting a quick pace at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast time' suggests speed, but it is a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to ease up or soften in severity, much as a grip or effort slackens.

clue.text: Requiring unusual strength to turn it — I can't

indicators.note: to turn something over is to churn it about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged, ignoring dash and apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone grunts that they cannot turn a stiff handle without enormous force.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means colossal, like the Titans of Greek myth, so a titanic task needs huge power.

clue.text: Everyone is in favour of this form of transport

indicators.note: is in places one word inside another

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole group supports this way of travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In favour of' looks like a phrase meaning supporting; it splits into the container signal and the favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-air balloon carries passengers through the sky, so it is one kind of transport.

clue.text: Kind of government found in African country

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so one letter is placed within the country's name

parts.note: Benin is a West African nation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A particular type of regime is discovered in an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of government' reads as type of regime; 'Kind' is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means gentle and well-meaning toward others, matching the adjective sense of a kindly person.

clue.text: It's no longer needed to complete a sentence

definitions.text: It's no longer needed to complete a sentence

parts.words: It's no longer needed to complete a sentence
parts.note: surface reading: a word that is redundant in grammar
setter's reading: a judicial sentence of death carried out by hanging, now abolished

explanation.walkthrough: The sentence is a court's death sentence, not a line of grammar; the device for carrying it out is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbet is a gallows where executions were carried out and bodies displayed, made redundant by the end of capital punishment.

clue.text: Fickle Conservative spotted in a moment

indicators.note: something spotted in a place is seen inside it, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: an instant is a moment
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A changeable Tory politician is caught out in a fleeting moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconstant describes someone whose loyalties or feelings keep changing, the same as being fickle.

clue.text: Drink at home with Bond

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
someone who is in is at home

explanation.surface: James Bond enjoys a drink in his own home.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised Bond suggests 007, but it is the restraint. Cha, or char, is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain links things together or restrains a prisoner, just as a bond ties or fetters.

clue.text: Essential to curb earl's support

indicators.note: essential means at the core, so the letters lie within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A restraint on an aristocrat is vital to keeping him in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to hold it up, so the verb is a direct synonym of support.

clue.text: Desire causes a fascinating woman to lose her head

indicators.note: losing the head means dropping the first letter of the word

parts.note: a bewitching, enchanting woman

explanation.surface: Longing makes an alluring woman behave foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: To lose one's head usually means to panic, but here it drops W from WITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving to do something, a figurative sense of an urge or desire.

clue.text: It's a code word for 'excellent'

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word for B in the NATO phonetic alphabet
second meaning: a shout of approval

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a secret signal meaning 'excellent'; in fact the word is both the radio code for B and a cry of applause.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the NATO spelling-alphabet name for B and an exclamation of praise like well done.

clue.text: Cover for the retired

parts.note: surface reading: insurance or protection for pensioners
setter's reading: people who have gone to bed for the night

explanation.walkthrough: Retired suggests pensioners and cover suggests insurance; here retired means gone to bed and cover is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This loose garment is worn in bed, covering people who have retired for the night.

clue.text: A number refuse to accept protecting the Head of Charterhouse shows bias

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: to protect something is to shield it all round, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: to deny is to refuse to accept

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is all that is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the school's name

explanation.surface: Several governors will not admit the headmaster of Charterhouse, a famous English public school, which reveals prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is an inclination or leaning toward something, which is what a bias amounts to.

clue.text: Opportunity for revolutionary to embrace a South African political party

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one name goes around the other

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist guerrilla
the African National Congress

explanation.surface: A chance for a radical to throw his support behind the ANC.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is a favourable occasion or opening to do something, the same as an opportunity.
